- **Plant part:** A wheat/grass leaf blade, viewed in close-up
- **Color pattern:** The leaf shows yellowing (chlorosis) along the upper portion, with orange-brown to reddish-brown discoloration concentrated in linear stripes running parallel to the leaf veins
- **Pattern characteristics:** The lesions appear as elongated, stripe-like bands following the vein direction — classic for a stripe/yellow rust pattern
- **Pustule appearance:** The orange coloration appears as streaked, elongated lesion bands rather than round discrete pustules (which would suggest leaf rust)
- **Distribution:** The coloration is organized in linear, longitudinal streaks running the full length of the leaf — very characteristic of **Stripe Rust** (also called Yellow Rust, *Puccinia striiformis*)

**Reasoning:**

- Stripe Rust produces linear, yellow-orange to orange pustules arranged in stripes parallel to leaf veins — exactly what is visible here
- Wheat Leaf Rust (*P. triticina*) produces rounder, more scattered uredinia — not seen here
- Stem Rust produces larger, brick-red pustules on stems — not matching
- The stripe pattern rules out tan spot, septoria (which show tan/brown blotch lesions), and powdery mildew (white powdery growth)
- The linear orange streaking is the hallmark of Stripe Rust
